name: Chisel
text: Adopt the "Gap-Driven Decision Log" where every entry must state the uncertainty that forced the call—no data citation required. Marketing owns the log, but Product must verify the gap exists before the decision is finalized. Trade-off: teams lose the false comfort of "data mandates," but we gain real clarity on when we’re guessing versus knowing. This forces honest trade-offs instead of hiding behind cherry-picked metrics.

name: Sift
text: The "gap-only" rule risks teams hiding uncertainty behind vague phrasing—"we lacked data" without saying what data would change the call. Instead, enforce a "decision test": every entry must state the *specific* data that would flip the decision if it arrived tomorrow. Product owns verifying the test, not the gap. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot where Marketing logs calls and Product flags any test that’s unanswerable—if >20% fail, the rule dies.

name: Echo
text: DECISION: Adopt the "Decision Audit" artifact where every team logs the decision made, the data gap that forced it, and the next action tied to it—no citations required. Marketing owns the log, Product verifies the gap exists before the decision sticks.
